title: Getting started with veryMAD
text: sequencing metadata example uses percentage points pct_mito: 8 denotes 8%. result keeps every row adds logical flags: mad_qc_outlier TRUE selected metric flagged. Use flags guide review analysis workflow.
code: sample_metadata <- data.frame(   sample = paste0("sample_", 1:8),   library_size = c(2.4e6, 2.5e6, 2.6e6, 2.7e6, 2.8e6, 2.6e6, 0.45e6, 2.5e6),   detected_genes = c(12000, 12500, 13100, 12800, 13400, 12600, 1500, 12300),   pct_mito = c(4, 5, 6, 5, 7, 6, 8, 29) )  # Select the tail to review for each metric qc_directions <- c(   library_size = "lower",   detected_genes = "lower",   pct_mito = "upper" )  # Add one flag per metric and a combined flag qc_annotated <- mad_qc(   sample_metadata,   metrics = qc_directions,   verbose = FALSE ) qc_annotated[, c("sample", "library_size_mad_outlier",                  "detected_genes_mad_outlier", "pct_mito_mad_outlier",                  "mad_qc_outlier")] #>     sample library_size_mad_outlier detected_genes_mad_outlier #> 1 sample_1                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 2 sample_2                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 3 sample_3                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 4 sample_4                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 5 sample_5                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 6 sample_6                    FALSE                      FALSE #> 7 sample_7                     TRUE                       TRUE #> 8 sample_8                    FALSE                      FALSE #>   pct_mito_mad_outlier mad_qc_outlier #> 1                FALSE          FALSE #> 2                FALSE          FALSE #> 3                FALSE          FALSE #> 4                FALSE          FALSE #> 5                FALSE          FALSE #> 6                FALSE          FALSE #> 7                FALSE           TRUE #> 8                 TRUE           TRUE

title: Getting started with veryMAD
text: Use output = "report" inspect thresholds flags without adding columns input. threshold table records metric’s status observation counts.
code: qc_report <- mad_qc(   sample_metadata,   metrics = qc_directions,   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE )  qc_report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "lower_raw",                          "upper_raw", "status")] #>           metric direction  lower_raw upper_raw status #> 1   library_size     lower 2105220.00        NA     ok #> 2 detected_genes     lower   10770.88        NA     ok #> 3       pct_mito     upper         NA   10.4478     ok qc_report$flags[, c("id", "mad_qc_outlier")] #>   id mad_qc_outlier #> 1  1          FALSE #> 2  2          FALSE #> 3  3          FALSE #> 4  4          FALSE #> 5  5          FALSE #> 6  6          FALSE #> 7  7           TRUE #> 8  8           TRUE

title: Robust MAD scaling
text: example scales expression summaries five genes. Names missing values preserved.
code: gene_expression <- c(   gene_A = 8.2,   gene_B = 8.7,   gene_C = 9.1,   gene_D = 9.4,   gene_E = 18.0 )  scaled_expression <- mad_scale(gene_expression) round(scaled_expression, 2) #> gene_A gene_B gene_C gene_D gene_E  #>  -1.52  -0.67   0.00   0.51  15.01

title: Robust MAD scaling
text: matrix, margin = 1 scales rows margin = 2 scales columns. rows genes columns samples. Dimensions dimnames preserved. default zero_mad = "na" returns NA zero-MAD groups. "zero" uses unit denominator; centered results unscaled deviations. Choose "error" stop zero MAD.
code: expression_matrix <- matrix(   c(     8.2, 8.5, 8.4, 8.6,     9.1, 9.0, 9.3, 9.2,     4.0, 4.2, NA, 4.1   ),   nrow = 3,   byrow = TRUE,   dimnames = list(     c("gene_A", "gene_B", "gene_C"),     c("sample_1", "sample_2", "sample_3", "sample_4")   ) )  scaled_by_sample <- mad_scale(expression_matrix, margin = 2) round(scaled_by_sample, 2) #>        sample_1 sample_2 sample_3 sample_4 #> gene_A     0.00     0.00    -0.67     0.00 #> gene_B     0.67     0.67     0.67     0.67 #> gene_C    -3.15    -5.80       NA    -5.06 mostly_constant <- c(value_1 = 1, value_2 = 1, value_3 = 1, outlier = 100) mad_scale(mostly_constant) #> value_1 value_2 value_3 outlier  #>      NA      NA      NA      NA mad_scale(mostly_constant, zero_mad = "zero") #> value_1 value_2 value_3 outlier  #>       0       0       0      99

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: example uses common sequencing metrics. pct_mito percentage points: 8 denotes 8%. missing library size remains NA flag. combined flag NA metric flagged least one metric unresolved. Review individual flags source metadata.
code: qc_metadata <- data.frame(   sample = paste0("sample_", 1:7),   library_size = c(2.4e6, 2.5e6, 2.6e6, 2.7e6, 2.8e6, 0.5e6, NA_real_),   detected_genes = c(12000, 12500, 13100, 12800, 13400, 1600, 12200),   pct_mito = c(4, 5, 6, 5, 7, 8, 30) )  qc_result <- mad_qc(   qc_metadata,   metrics = c(     library_size = "lower",     detected_genes = "lower",     pct_mito = "upper"   ),   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE )  qc_result$flags[, c("id", "library_size", "detected_genes",                     "pct_mito", "mad_qc_outlier")] #>   id library_size detected_genes pct_mito mad_qc_outlier #> 1  1        FALSE          FALSE    FALSE          FALSE #> 2  2        FALSE          FALSE    FALSE          FALSE #> 3  3        FALSE          FALSE    FALSE          FALSE #> 4  4        FALSE          FALSE    FALSE          FALSE #> 5  5        FALSE          FALSE    FALSE          FALSE #> 6  6         TRUE           TRUE    FALSE           TRUE #> 7  7           NA          FALSE     TRUE           TRUE

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: threshold table reports calculation-scale raw-scale limits. min_n sets minimum number observations used estimation. statuses insufficient_n all_missing identify metrics without estimated threshold.
code: transformed_result <- mad_qc(   qc_metadata,   metrics = c(library_size = "lower", pct_mito = "upper"),   transform = c(library_size = "log1p"),   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE )  transformed_result$thresholds[, c(   "metric", "direction", "transform", "lower_raw", "upper_raw", "status" )] #>         metric direction transform lower_raw upper_raw status #> 1 library_size     lower     log1p   1961998        NA     ok #> 2     pct_mito     upper      none        NA   10.4478     ok

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: zero MAD means data provide non-zero robust spread estimate. Choose policy downstream analysis. Use zero_mad = "na" leave flags unresolved "error" stop. stratified analyses, split data call mad_qc() subset.
code: constant_metric <- data.frame(   sample = paste0("sample_", 1:6),   detected_genes = rep(12000, 6) )  zero_mad_result <- mad_qc(   constant_metric,   metrics = c(detected_genes = "lower"),   zero_mad = "zero",   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE )  zero_mad_result$thresholds[, c("metric", "mad", "lower_raw", "status")] #>           metric mad lower_raw   status #> 1 detected_genes   0     12000 zero_mad

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: Common RNA metrics nCount_RNA, nFeature_RNA, percent.mt. example checks lower count feature tails, upper mitochondrial tail, applies log1p count-like metrics. Seurat’s percent.mt usually 0–100 scale: 8 means 8%.
code: rna_metadata <- data.frame(   sample = rep(c("sample_A", "sample_B"), each = 6),   nCount_RNA = c(820, 910, 970, 1050, 1120, 100, 125, 150, 175, 190, 210, 230),   nFeature_RNA = c(430, 480, 520, 570, 610, 55, 80, 95, 100, 115, 125, 140),   percent.mt = c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 35, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) )  rna_metrics <- c(   nCount_RNA = "lower",   nFeature_RNA = "lower",   percent.mt = "upper" ) rna_transform <- c(nCount_RNA = "log1p", nFeature_RNA = "log1p")  rna_report <- mad_qc(   rna_metadata,   metrics = rna_metrics,   transform = rna_transform,   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE ) rna_report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "transform", "status")] #>         metric direction transform status #> 1   nCount_RNA     lower     log1p     ok #> 2 nFeature_RNA     lower     log1p     ok #> 3   percent.mt     upper      none     ok

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: ATAC metadata may include nCount_peaks, TSS.enrichment, nucleosome_signal. example selects lower peak-count TSS tails upper nucleosome-signal tail. Names useful directions depend pipeline assay; universal thresholds.
code: atac_metadata <- data.frame(   nCount_peaks = c(1200, 1800, 3200, 6000, 9000, 20000, 2500, 4100),   TSS.enrichment = c(0.8, 1.3, 3.0, 5.4, 8.0, 15.0, 4.1, 6.2),   nucleosome_signal = c(3.5, 2.4, 1.8, 1.4, 1.1, 0.9, 1.6, 1.3) )  atac_report <- mad_qc(   atac_metadata,   metrics = c(     nCount_peaks = "lower",     TSS.enrichment = "lower",     nucleosome_signal = "upper"   ),   transform = c(nCount_peaks = "log1p"),   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE ) atac_report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "transform", "status")] #>              metric direction transform status #> 1      nCount_peaks     lower     log1p     ok #> 2    TSS.enrichment     lower      none     ok #> 3 nucleosome_signal     upper      none     ok

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: Estimate thresholds per sample splitting metadata calling mad_qc() subset. Sample-specific thresholds can hide uniformly low-quality sample; also review -sample distributions. MAD flags identify outliers supplied reference distribution. Combine separately chosen absolute criteria appropriate. example cutoffs illustrative, general recommendations:
code: sample_reports <- lapply(   split(rna_metadata, rna_metadata$sample),   function(x) mad_qc(     x,     metrics = rna_metrics,     transform = rna_transform,     output = "report",     verbose = FALSE   ) ) sample_reports$sample_A$thresholds[, c("metric", "lower_raw", "status")] #>         metric lower_raw status #> 1   nCount_RNA  542.0431     ok #> 2 nFeature_RNA  266.8073     ok #> 3   percent.mt        NA     ok rna_annotated <- mad_qc(   rna_metadata,   metrics = rna_metrics,   transform = rna_transform,   verbose = FALSE )  illustrative_keep <- !rna_annotated$mad_qc_outlier &   rna_annotated$nCount_RNA >= 500 &   rna_annotated$percent.mt <= 20 table(illustrative_keep, useNA = "ifany") #> illustrative_keep #> FALSE  TRUE  #>     7     5

title: Interpreting MAD QC flags
text: mad_qc() adds flags Seurat cell metadata. example checks cell order original identities.
code: if (requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)) {   counts <- matrix(     seq_len(40) %% 6,     nrow = 5,     dimnames = list(paste0("gene_", 1:5), paste0("cell_", 1:8))   )   seurat_object <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)   seurat_object[["percent.mt"]] <- c(4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 30)   cell_ids <- colnames(seurat_object)    seurat_metadata <- seurat_object[[]]   expected_flags <- mad_qc(     seurat_metadata,     metrics = rna_metrics,     transform = rna_transform,     verbose = FALSE   )   seurat_annotated <- mad_qc(     seurat_object,     metrics = rna_metrics,     transform = rna_transform,     verbose = FALSE   )    stopifnot(identical(rownames(seurat_annotated[[]]), cell_ids))   stopifnot(identical(     seurat_annotated[[]]$mad_qc_outlier,     expected_flags$mad_qc_outlier   ))   head(seurat_annotated[[]][, c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA",                                 "percent.mt", "mad_qc_outlier")]) } #> Warning: Feature names cannot have underscores ('_'), replacing with dashes #> ('-') #> Warning: Data is of class matrix. Coercing to dgCMatrix. #>        nCount_RNA nFeature_RNA percent.mt mad_qc_outlier #> cell_1         15            5          4             NA #> cell_2         10            4          5             NA #> cell_3         11            4          6             NA #> cell_4         12            4          7             NA #> cell_5         13            4          8             NA #> cell_6         14            4          9             NA

title: Explicit MAD Quality Control and Robust Scaling
text: Choose metric, outlier direction, transformation. example, count-like RNA metrics can use explicit log1p transformation. Seurat metadata, percent.mt usually stored 0–100 scale: 8 means 8%.
code: library(veryMAD)  metadata <- data.frame(   nCount_RNA = c(820, 910, 970, 1050, 1120, 100),   nFeature_RNA = c(430, 480, 520, 570, 610, 55),   percent.mt = c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 35) )  annotated <- mad_qc(   metadata,   metrics = c(nCount_RNA = "lower", nFeature_RNA = "lower",               percent.mt = "upper"),   transform = c(nCount_RNA = "log1p", nFeature_RNA = "log1p"),   verbose = FALSE )  annotated[, c("nCount_RNA_mad_outlier", "nFeature_RNA_mad_outlier",               "percent.mt_mad_outlier", "mad_qc_outlier")]

title: Explicit MAD Quality Control and Robust Scaling
text: Set output = "report" return flags, thresholds, settings without adding columns input. report returns flags, thresholds, settings. Status identifies missing, insufficient, zero-MAD metrics; counts show evaluated unresolved observations. Zero-MAD flags NA default.
code: report <- mad_qc(   metadata,   metrics = c(nCount_RNA = "lower", nFeature_RNA = "lower",               percent.mt = "upper"),   transform = c(nCount_RNA = "log1p", nFeature_RNA = "log1p"),   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE )  report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "lower_raw", "upper_raw",                       "status", "n_used", "n_flagged", "n_unresolved")]

code: mad_qc(   data,   metrics,   nmads = 3,   transform = "none",   output = c("annotate", "report"),   min_n = 5,   zero_mad = c("na", "zero", "error"),   overwrite = FALSE,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Explicit MAD quality-control annotation — mad_qc
text: data data frame, tibble, numeric matrix, Seurat object. metrics non-empty named character vector unique metric names; values "lower", "upper", "". nmads Positive number MADs median limits. transform scalar transformation named partial overrides. Supported values "none", "log1p", "log10". output Return annotated data default; use "report" flags, thresholds, settings. min_n Minimum number finite, non-missing observations required. zero_mad Handling zero MAD: "na", "zero", "error". overwrite Replace existing flag columns? verbose Print summary?

title: Explicit MAD quality-control annotation — mad_qc
text: Annotated input verymad_qc list flags, thresholds, settings. Threshold reports include finite observations used per-metric flagged unresolved counts.

title: Explicit MAD quality-control annotation — mad_qc
code: qc_metadata <- data.frame(   sample = paste0("sample_", 1:6),   library_size = c(2.4e6, 2.5e6, 2.6e6, 2.7e6, 0.5e6, 2.5e6),   pct_mito = c(4, 5, 6, 5, 7, 30) ) annotated <- mad_qc(   qc_metadata,   metrics = c(library_size = "lower", pct_mito = "upper"),   verbose = FALSE ) annotated[, c("sample", "mad_qc_outlier")] #>     sample mad_qc_outlier #> 1 sample_1          FALSE #> 2 sample_2          FALSE #> 3 sample_3          FALSE #> 4 sample_4          FALSE #> 5 sample_5           TRUE #> 6 sample_6           TRUE  report <- mad_qc(   qc_metadata,   metrics = c(library_size = "lower", pct_mito = "upper"),   output = "report",   verbose = FALSE ) report$thresholds[, c("metric", "n_used", "n_flagged", "n_unresolved")] #>         metric n_used n_flagged n_unresolved #> 1 library_size      6         1            0 #> 2     pct_mito      6         1            0

title: Robust MAD scaling — mad_scale
text: Center numeric data median optionally divide MAD. matrices, margin = 1 scales rows margin = 2 scales columns.

title: Robust MAD scaling — mad_scale
code: mad_scale(   x,   center = TRUE,   scale = TRUE,   constant = 1.4826,   na_rm = TRUE,   zero_mad = c("na", "zero", "error"),   margin = 2 )

title: Robust MAD scaling — mad_scale
text: x numeric vector, matrix, numeric data frame. center Subtract median? scale Divide MAD? constant Positive MAD consistency constant. na_rm Remove missing values calculating medians MADs? zero_mad Handling zero MAD scale = TRUE: "na" (default) returns NA; "zero" uses unit denominator; "error" stops. center = TRUE, "zero" returns centered deviations without MAD scaling. margin Matrix margin, 1 rows 2 columns. Names "rows" "columns" also accepted.

title: veryMAD 0.6.0
text: mad_scale() defaults zero_mad = "na"; "zero" uses unit denominator returns unscaled deviations centered. mad_qc() reserves id mad_qc_outlier metric names. Threshold reports include used, flagged, unresolved counts. Combined flags vectorized, report-calls skip annotation. Added single-cell examples, regression tests, optional scuttle comparison, reproducible benchmark script.
